checks: Read the changed lines in the context of the surrounding file and confirm the diff does what its commit or change description intends.
Check correctness risks: missing error handling, unchecked nullable values, boundary and empty-input cases, and partial state left behind on failure.
Check security risks introduced by the change: untrusted input reaching a sensitive sink, credentials or personal data in code or logs, and missing authorization checks.
Check performance risks: repeated work, unbounded loops or allocations, and blocking calls on a hot path.
Check maintainability problems: misleading names, duplicated constants or branches, and comments that no longer match the code.
Check whether the behavior change is covered by a test, and whether an existing test still asserts the old behavior.
Report redundant or dead code only when the change creates a real behavior, maintenance or evolution risk.

rules.description: General correctness checks for program source files.
checks: Check every return and failure path: errors are surfaced, propagated or handled, and no success value is produced after a failure.
Check nullable and boundary inputs: empty collections, zero values, missing optional fields, first and last elements, and off-by-one ranges.
Check state and ordering: shared mutable state, partial updates on failure, and asynchronous work that can race, leak or run after cleanup.
Check the changed contract against its callers and implementations: parameters, return shape, thrown errors and defaults stay consistent.

rules.description: TypeScript and JavaScript runtime hazards that the type checker does not catch.
checks: Check type escapes: any, non-null assertions and casts that hide a runtime shape mismatch rather than prove it.
Check async code: unhandled promise rejections, missing awaits, and callbacks that can run more than once.
Check runtime API contracts: encoding, path handling, error codes and cleanup around I/O or subprocesses.

rules.description: Go error, context and concurrency hazards.
checks: Check error handling: errors are wrapped with context, never discarded, and compared with errors.Is or errors.As where the caller depends on the cause.
Check goroutine and resource lifetime: cancellation is propagated through context, closers are deferred, and no goroutine can outlive its caller.
Check shared state for data races and lock ordering, including maps and slices captured by closures.

rules.description: Python exception, mutation and async hazards.
checks: Check exception scope: broad except clauses, swallowed exceptions, and cleanup that only runs on the success path.
Check mutable default arguments, mutation while iterating, and blocking calls inside async functions.

rules.description: Java and Kotlin nullability, resource and concurrency hazards.
checks: Check nullability and resource lifecycle: try-with-resources, closable streams, and Kotlin platform types received from Java APIs.
Check concurrency: shared mutable state, thread safety of injected dependencies, and blocking work on an event-loop thread.

rules.description: Rust panic, error and ownership hazards.
checks: Check panic paths: unwrap or expect on data that can be absent or invalid, and integer casts that can truncate.
Check ownership and errors: unnecessary clones, lost error context, and unsafe blocks without a stated invariant.

rules.description: Impact of a removed file or symbol.
checks: Confirm every reference to the removed file or symbol is updated: imports, build targets, routing or configuration entries, tests and documentation.
Confirm removing public behavior is intentional and that no runtime path still expects the old module.
Confirm deleted configuration or assets are no longer referenced by deployment or packaging.

rules.description: Schema and data migration safety.
checks: Check forward and rollback paths, including data backfill and what happens when only part of the migration succeeds.
Check locks and long-running statements against production table size and traffic.
Check that the schema change stays compatible with the previous application version during a rolling deploy.

rules.description: Configuration changes must match the code that reads them.
checks: Trace each changed configuration key or default to the code that reads it; confirm the name, type and fallback value agree.
Check environment parity: development, test and production configuration stay compatible with the change.
Check that behavior enabled or disabled by the change has a matching test or a documented manual step.

rules.description: Application security checks for program source files.
checks: Trace untrusted input to sensitive sinks: command execution, SQL, templates, file paths, deserialization and outbound requests.
Check authorization and authentication on every new entry point, not only on the UI path.
Check secrets and personal data: no credentials in code, logs, error messages or test fixtures.
Check path, URL and header construction for traversal and injection, including redirects and file uploads.

rules.description: Secrets, permissions and exposure in configuration and CI.
checks: Check for plaintext credentials and tokens in configuration, CI definitions and test data.
Check permissions and exposure: overly broad CI tokens, permissive CORS, public buckets and debug endpoints.
Check that third-party actions and images are pinned and that new network endpoints are expected.

rules.description: Dependency manifest and lockfile changes.
checks: Check that the manifest and lockfile change together and that no unrelated dependency was upgraded.
Check version ranges and resolved versions for unexpected major jumps or prerelease builds.
Check whether a newly added package is required; prefer an existing dependency or the standard library when it is sufficient.

rules.description: Cost introduced by changed code paths.
checks: Check the cost of new loops and lookups; flag work that grows with input where the old path did not.
Check repeated I/O, parsing or serialization inside loops that can be hoisted or batched.
Check unbounded concurrency, caches and buffers introduced by the change.

rules.description: Build, CI and runtime configuration cost.
checks: Check build or CI changes for repeated installs, full rebuilds or disabled caches that slow feedback.
Check runtime configuration defaults that can cause unbounded retries, timeouts or pool sizes.

rules.description: Readability and evolution cost of changed code.
checks: Check names, structure and comments against the surrounding code; the change should read like the file it lands in.
Check the public surface: a new exported function, option or type needs a reason and a usable name.
Check comments and documentation touched by the change for accuracy; remove claims the code no longer supports.
Check error messages and logs for enough context to diagnose the failure without a debugger.

rules.description: Documentation accuracy and drift.
checks: Check that documented commands, flags, paths and examples still match the code.
Check links and version references; prefer a stable reference over an exact line or transient identifier.

rules.description: Readability and drift in configuration files.
checks: Check duplicated keys and drift between environments or CI jobs.
Check that commented-out or dead configuration is removed or explained.
Check names and grouping against the neighboring configuration.

rules.description: Test coverage of changed behavior.
checks: Identify the behavior the diff changes and find the test that pins it; if none exists, say what should be tested.
Check new branches, error paths and boundary values for coverage by a concrete test.
Check that existing tests were updated for intentional behavior changes instead of deleted or weakened.

rules.description: Quality and reliability of changed tests.
checks: Check that the test fails for the bug or missing behavior it claims to cover; remove or fix assertions that cannot fail.
Check isolation and determinism: shared state, time, ordering, network and filesystem assumptions.
Check that mocks match the real contract and are not hiding a broken integration.

rules.description: Duplication and dead code with a real maintenance risk.
checks: Look for a second implementation of logic that already exists in the repository; reuse it or document why a separate copy is needed.
Look for dead branches, unused exports and leftover compatibility paths created by the change.
Report duplication only when it creates a maintenance or correctness risk; do not restate style preferences.

rules.description: Fixed checks for the cross-file unit; the unit is generated deterministically, not by an agent.
checks: Trace each changed interface, exported symbol or data shape to its callers and confirm every caller is updated.
Check configuration and behavior consistency: changed defaults, environment names and feature flags must match the code that reads them.
Check test impact across the change: which test units and fixtures must change, and which existing assertions now contradict the change.
Check deleted or renamed files and symbols for remaining references in code, build files, packaging and documentation.
Check for duplicate or parallel implementations introduced across the changed files and decide whether they create a real risk.
Check the overall diff for an incomplete change: one side of a contract updated without the other.
